t: You're on Basinghall Street, a street in the City of London. It lies mostly in the ward of Bassishaw, with the southern end in Cheap and Coleman Street wards. The street and the ward take their name from the Bassing family, who built a hall house here in the thirteenth century and were given certain privileges by the King. Charles Brooke, a British politician who lived from 1760 to 1833, lived on this street, which ties it to the political life of the period.
